The camera is positioned at a mid-range distance, framing Attila the Hun from head to hips, ensuring that his entire hat, large head, and hip area are clearly visible. Attila, the infamous Turko-Mongol warlord, is a short, squat man with a large head, yet his muscular, fit build and strong posture make him a figure of intimidating power. His East Asian features—deep-set, almond-shaped eyes, a flat nose, and high cheekbones—give him a harsh, battle-worn look. His facial hair is almost non-existent, with just a slight, faint mustache and a barely noticeable patchy beard along his chin, leaving his face mostly bare, which sharpens his intense expression.

Atop his head is a fur-lined Phrygian cap, with its soft, rounded top that leans forward. The thick fur trim circles the brim, adding a nomadic, warrior-like element to his look. His long, straight black hair flows freely past his shoulders, unadorned, giving him a wild, untamed appearance, further reflecting his status as a barbaric leader.

The camera captures his upper body and hips, showcasing his robust warrior attire. Attila wears a dark brown leather tunic, reinforced with interlocking leather armor plates that cover his chest and waist. His wide black leather belt, secured tightly around his hips, emphasizes his muscular build and readiness for battle. Draped over his broad shoulders is a heavy fur-lined cloak, slightly frayed at the edges from many years of war and travel, giving him a rugged, battle-tested appearance.

With his hips fully visible, the shot focuses on his strong upper body and confident posture, leaving out his legs but emphasizing his torso and commanding stance. His arms, wrapped in leather bracers, rest confidently at his sides. His piercing eyes, filled with arrogance and cold calculation, seem to judge anyone who stands before him. His scarred and weathered face, along with his minimal facial hair, reflects a life of ruthless conquest. Despite his short stature, Attila's presence radiates intimidation, charisma, and power, commanding both fear and respect from all who encounter him.
